title: The Dainty China Country, part 2
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: But the strangest of all were the people who lived in this queer country. There were milkmaids and shepherdesses, with brightly colored bodices and golden spots all over their gowns; and princesses with most gorgeous frocks of silver and gold and purple; and shepherds dressed in knee breeches with pink and yellow and blue stripes down them, and golden buckles on their shoes; and princes with jeweled crowns upon their heads, wearing ermine robes and satin doublets; and funny clowns in ruffled gowns, with round red spots upon their cheeks and tall, pointed caps. And, strangest of all, these people were all made of china, even to their clothes, and were so small that the tallest of them was no higher than Dorothy’s knee.

No one did so much as look at the travelers at first, except one little purple china dog with an extra-large head, which came to the wall and barked at them in a tiny voice, afterwards running away again.
“How shall we get down?” asked Dorothy.

They found the ladder so heavy they could not pull it up, so the Scarecrow fell off the wall and the others jumped down upon him so that the hard floor would not hurt their feet. Of course they took pains not to light on his head and get the pins in their feet. When all were safely down they picked up the Scarecrow, whose body was quite flattened out, and patted his straw into shape again.
“We must cross this strange place in order to get to the other side,” said Dorothy, “for it would be unwise for us to go any other way except due South.”

They began walking through the country of the china people, and the first thing they came to was a china milkmaid milking a china cow. As they drew near, the cow suddenly gave a kick and kicked over the stool, the pail, and even the milkmaid herself, and all fell on the china ground with a great clatter.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how tall were the china people?
options: No higher than Dorothy's knee
About as tall as Dorothy herself
Taller than the Tin Woodman
No bigger than Dorothy's thumb

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what came to the wall and barked at them?
options: A little purple china dog
A china cow with a broken leg
One of the china clowns
A shepherdess in a bright bodice

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did they get down from the wall?
options: The Scarecrow fell first and the others jumped on him
They pulled the ladder up and lowered it down
The Lion jumped down and caught each of them
They climbed down the smooth china face

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did they take pains to avoid?
options: Landing on the Scarecrow's head and the pins
Treading on the little china people
Breaking the ladder they had made
Waking the purple china dog again

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did they come to first in the country?
options: A china milkmaid milking a china cow
A church made of white china
A princess in a gorgeous frock
A clown standing on his head

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Scarecrow go off the wall first?
options: His body could break the others' fall without harm
He was the ruler and had to lead the way
He wanted to see the china people closely
He had dropped the basket over the edge

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why must they cross the china country at all?
options: Going any way but due south would be unwise
The china people had invited them through
The wall behind them could not be climbed again
Glinda's castle stood on the far side of it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what happened when they drew near the cow?
options: It kicked over the stool, the pail, and the milkmaid
It walked away quietly into a china barn
It stood quite still and let them pass
It broke into pieces at the sound of their feet

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does clatter describe?
options: The noise of the china falling
The chatter of the china people
The rattle of the Woodman's joints
The barking of the purple dog

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A beautiful country turns out to be fragile the moment they enter it
A country of china people welcomes the travellers warmly
The travellers decide to go around the china country
The Scarecrow is broken past mending by the fall

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the china clowns wearing?
options: Ruffled gowns and tall pointed caps
Ermine robes and satin doublets
Knee breeches with coloured stripes
Frocks of silver, gold, and purple

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the princesses wear?
options: Gorgeous frocks of silver, gold, and purple
Bodices with golden spots
Jewelled crowns and ermine robes
Plain white china, undecorated

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did they do with the flattened Scarecrow?
options: Picked him up and patted his straw into shape
Left him lying until he recovered himself
Carried him the rest of the way
Stuffed him with fresh china dust

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why could they not bring the ladder down?
options: They found it too heavy to pull up the wall
The china people had taken it away
It had broken as the last of them climbed
The Woodman had left it in the forest

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what were the china people made of, clothes included?
options: China, every part of them
Painted wood over china frames
Silk and satin over china bodies
Straw, like the Scarecrow

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does queer describe about the country?
options: Strange and unlike anywhere else
Sad and rather gloomy
Crowded and full of noise
Poor and badly kept

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A first look at the china people, and a first accident among them
A friendly welcome from the people of the china country
The travellers' decision to turn back from the china wall
A search through the china country for a way out
